messages:
sara: heads-up — noticed steady mem growth on kv-cache host during longctx runs (>8k tokens). RSS up ~1.8GB over 90m, looks like KV pages not being reclaimed between requests.
liam: can you paste the perf profile or heap stats?
sara: quick snapshot from yesterday: `kv_resident_pages: 1_220_000 -> 1_480_000` and `kv_page_allocs:+260k` over 1.5h, tail latency stayed fine but overall memory keeps rising.
sara: repro command I used: `./bench --model=redwood-small --seq=8192 --concurrency=8 --duration=90m`
liam: hmm, that sequence length is where we hit longctx behaviors. any patterns on keys?
sara: yes — noticed many small prefixes being inserted, largely from our prompt templating lib that includes ephemeral session ids. keys looked like `sess:<tenant>:<ephemeral-id>:pref:<hash>` so high cardinality.
nisha: ephemeral ids will kill cache reuse. can we canonicalize sessionless prefixes?
sara: prototype change — strip ephemeral-id for prefix keying and attach session tag to request metadata instead. seems to increase reuse by ~30% in a quick run.
liam: nice. do you have flamegraph of the runtime during growth window?
sara: uploaded to the perf bucket: https://perf.redwood/s/graph/zk9a2 — shows persistent slab allocations inside kv_map::insert and page compaction not running often enough.
ish a: ops-bot alerted earlier about pagefault spikes around 03:10 UTC.
ops-bot: alert: host-gpu-07 kv_cache_pages 1.48M (threshold 1.2M) — auto-snapshot created /snapshots/5123456820
liam: two hypotheses: 1) key cardinality prevents reuse so pages are cold-lived; 2) compaction/eviction heuristics are TTL-based and longctx requests keep entries pinned.
sara: quick experiment: changed keyizer to drop ephemeral ids and set candidate_ttl=10m (was 60m). bench run showed resident pages stabilized and peak dropped ~400k.
liam: curious about eviction churn cost — did you see CPU impact from compaction?
sara: small bump in CPU (2-3%) during compaction windows, but overall token throughput improved due to better KV hit-rate (cache hit +22%).
nisha: important: we need to avoid changing application semantics by stripping ids. propose a mapping layer: normalized_key = if ephemeral_id in metadata then "__SESSIONLESS__" else keep full. that preserves behavior when app intentionally wants isolation.
liam: agree. also want to revisit key fingerprinting to make it path-insensitive: use FNV64 over normalized prefix and tenant salt.
sara: sample proto key code I ran:

func normalizePrefix(p Prefix) string {
  if p.EphemeralID != "" {
    return fmt.Sprintf("%s::%s::%s","__SESSIONLESS__", p.Tenant, p.PromptHash)
  }
  return fmt.Sprintf("%s::%s::%s", p.Tenant, p.SessionID, p.PromptHash)
}
key := fnv64(normalizePrefix(prefix) + ":v1")

liam: add versioning (`:v1`) is good for rolling changes. also add a per-tenant knob to opt back into strict session semantics.
sara: logging note — turned on `kv.debug.keying=true` during tests. produced ~3k unique normalized keys vs 18k before.
nisha: do we need to update eviction policy? If normalized keys increase reuse, eviction can be more LRU-friendly. maybe use a hotset window algorithm tuned for longctx: favor prefixes with >X reuses in last Y minutes.
liam: sketch of hotset rule: if reuse_count(key) >= 3 in last 10m pin strong, else candidate for eviction. should reduce fragmentation.
sara: one weird thing: fragmentation metric `kv_free_frag_ratio` still high on some hosts. I suspect slab allocator internal fragmentation when small pages dominate.
nisha: open a follow-up to eng-infra for heap-slab tuning. for now, central fixes: 1) normalized keying to reduce cardinality; 2) lower candidate_ttl for ephemeral-heavy tenants; 3) hotset pinning rule.
sara: rolling canary patch to staging now (build 2026.3.12-kvkeynorm). expecting CI-green then staged rollout.
ci-bot: deploy started for ref=2026.3.12-kvkeynorm -> staging (job #4521).
liam: once canary runs, I'll attach kernel scheduler trace to confirm we're not regressing on batching/kernel-selection due to added CPU work.
sara: thanks — will monitor mem, kv_resident_pages, and cache hit rate. sharing results later. :thumbsup:
liam: if this fixes reuse, we should add an SDK change note for prompt template authors about ephemeral ids.
sara: agreed. I'll draft a short devex PR and release note.
ops-bot: snapshot retained /snapshots/5123456820 tag:kv-triage
